mechanism_narrative: Continued week-on-week declines in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES mobility show commuter and workplace footfall are still contracting, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is greater than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A GROCERY_PHARM reading at or below -20.0 signals a shift to essential-only shopping trips; discretionary retail trips are crowded out, so RETAIL_REC will fall over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days is higher than its mean over the last 14 days when GROCERY_PHARM is <= -20.0.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL is positive while PARKS is below -15, residents are staying home instead of taking outdoor leisure trips; this suppresses retail-and-recreation excursions, so RETAIL_REC will decline over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 0 and PARKS < -15 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days is higher than its mean over the last 14 days when RESIDENTIAL is positive and PARKS is below -15.

mechanism_narrative: In a broad mobility contraction where TRANSIT is below -30 and WORKPLACES is below -35, retail footfall tracks the transit decline with a one-week lag, so RETAIL_REC will be lower next week.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT < -30 and WORKPLACES < -35 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 7 days is higher than its mean over the last 7 days.

mechanism_narrative: Late-August seasonal transition reduces outdoor leisure demand; PARKS staying below -20 with no rebound indicates weak excursion activity, so retail-and-recreation mobility will continue lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than its mean over the last 28 days while PARKS remains below -20.

mechanism_narrative: A positive RESIDENTIAL reading for two of the last four weeks indicates voluntary home confinement; as residents consolidate activity at home, retail-and-recreation trips are reduced, so RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than its mean over the last 28 days when RESIDENTIAL remains non-negative.

mechanism_narrative: A RETAIL_REC print at -40.0 combined with TRANSIT below -35 marks an exhaustion point in the decline; delayed discretionary trips produce a modest rebound, so RETAIL_REC will be higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC <= -40.0 and TRANSIT < -35 in the latest week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 14 days is lower than or equal to its mean over the last 14 days when RETAIL_REC is <= -40.0 and TRANSIT < -35.

mechanism_narrative: Policy tightening is visible as a greater than 5-point week-on-week fall in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES; this drags retail-and-recreation mobility down over the next week, so RETAIL_REC will be lower.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than 5 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES falls more than 5 points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -30.7 to -35.7 and WORKPLACES fell from -33.3 to -40.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 7 days is higher than its mean over the last 7 days while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both fall more than 5 points week-on-week.
